title: The History of The Sims | From SimCity To The Sims 4 Going Free | Gaming History
description: The full history of The Sims: Will Wright and Maxis, the first game in February 2000 that passed Myst, The Sims 2, The Sims 3, The Sims 4 in 2014 and the free to play launch in October 2022.

sections.heading: The game about everyday life
sections.script: Welcome back to the channel. Today we are going through the history of The Sims, the life simulation series where you build houses, create families and guide tiny people through their days. It is one of the most successful series ever made, and it began with a very unusual idea: a game with no final boss, no score to chase and no ending. We will start with the designer Will Wright and the studio Maxis, go through the first game in February two thousand, follow the sequels in two thousand four, two thousand nine and two thousand fourteen, and finish with the big day in October twenty twenty two when The Sims four became free. Every date here comes from Wikipedia and from news coverage and official pages for each release. Let us begin.

sections.heading: Will Wright and SimCity
sections.script: To understand The Sims, we have to start with its creator. Will Wright is a game designer and a co founder of the studio Maxis. Before The Sims, Maxis was known for simulation games that let you build and manage something big, and its most famous game was SimCity, which launched in nineteen eighty nine. In SimCity you manage a whole city, with roads, power and zones. That success proved that many players enjoyed games where they build and experiment instead of simply win or lose. It also gave Wright the confidence for a stranger idea: what if, instead of a city, the game let you manage the lives of a few ordinary people, living in a house that you design yourself?

sections.heading: Maxis joins Electronic Arts
sections.script: By the late nineties, Maxis had grown into a well known studio, and in nineteen ninety seven it was acquired by Electronic Arts, the company that still publishes the series today. That change mattered a great deal for the new project. A game about daily routines, like cooking, sleeping and visiting neighbours, looked very different from the action games of that period. With a large publisher behind it, the team could build something that treated everyday life as the real adventure. That is the setting in which Will Wright's idea became a finished game, and it is why the series has always carried the Electronic Arts name on its releases, as it does today.

sections.heading: The Sims arrives in February two thousand
sections.script: The Sims was released for Windows in North America on the fourth of February, two thousand, with a European release about a week later and a Japanese release in April. You created a family, built a home, and tried to keep your Sims happy by managing needs like hunger, energy and social life. The game had no fixed goal, and that was exactly the point. Players invented their own stories, from tidy dream homes to chaotic disasters. History dot com marks the fourth of February as the day the game was released, and it quickly became a very big hit.

sections.heading: Passing Myst
sections.script: The first Sims game did something remarkable. According to Wikipedia, by the twenty second of March, two thousand two, The Sims had sold more than six point three million copies worldwide, which made it the best selling PC game in history at that time, passing the adventure game Myst from nineteen ninety three. GameSpot covered the milestone under the headline that The Sims overtakes Myst. Sales numbers in this industry are often disputed, because publishers rarely release exact figures game by game, so it is fair to treat that record as a widely reported one. Still, the point is clear. A quiet game about daily life became one of the biggest computer games of its era.

sections.heading: Expansion packs and the Sims habit
sections.script: One reason the first game stayed popular for so long was the way it grew. The Sims was followed by a long list of expansion packs, each one adding new places to visit, new objects and new things to do. This habit became a signature of the series. Instead of replacing the whole game every few years, The Sims kept adding to it, so that players could build a bigger and more personal version over time. It is also why the series has so many fans who feel strongly about their favourite pack. We will not list them all, because there are far too many, but the idea of a game you keep expanding is central to how The Sims works.

sections.heading: The Sims 2 in two thousand four
sections.script: The Sims two was released for Windows on the fourteenth of September, two thousand four, developed by Maxis and published by Electronic Arts. It moved the series from flat, two dimensional pictures to full three dimensional graphics, and it let Sims grow through life stages, so you could follow a family across generations. The sequel also made the idea of a family story much stronger, because your choices now carried forward as children grew up. Many fans still remember it as a very warm and creative entry. A European release came a few days after the American one, so the exact date depends on where you lived, but the main launch is the fourteenth of September.

sections.heading: The Sims 3 and the open neighbourhood
sections.script: The Sims three launched on the second of June, two thousand nine, developed by the Redwood Shores studio of Maxis and published by Electronic Arts. The sequel had been announced back in November two thousand six. Its biggest change was the open neighbourhood. Instead of loading a lot, your Sims could walk through the whole town, meet people, visit shops and go to work without a break in the game. That made the world feel alive and connected. Many players loved this freedom, and The Sims three is still remembered as a very ambitious entry, because it tried to make the entire town into one big living space.

sections.heading: The Sims 4 and the free to play day
sections.script: The Sims four was released for Windows on the second of September, two thousand fourteen. The Mac version followed in February twenty fifteen, and PlayStation four and Xbox One versions arrived in November twenty seventeen. Then, in twenty twenty two, came a big change. According to the official EA help page, The Sims four became free to play on the eighteenth of October, twenty twenty two, on PC, Mac, Steam and PlayStation, and news sites covered it as a major move after eight years of paid sales. The base game became free to download, while expansion content stayed on sale. It was a smart way to bring in new players, many of whom were curious about the series.

sections.heading: Why The Sims lasts
sections.script: So why has The Sims lasted for more than twenty five years? A big part of the answer is that it never asked you to be good at it. There is no right way to play. Some people tell serious stories, some decorate houses for hours, and some like to see what funny things happen. Each sequel changed the look and the tools, but the heart of the idea stayed the same, and that idea first appeared in two thousand. Wikipedia lists the series as one of the best selling game franchises ever. We will not repeat a precise sales figure, since totals vary by source, but it is clear that few games have kept such a wide and loyal audience.

sections.heading: Which Sims game is your favourite
sections.script: That was the history of The Sims, from SimCity and Will Wright to the free to play launch of The Sims four in October twenty twenty two. Now over to you. Which game in the series did you play first, and which one is your favourite, the original, The Sims two, The Sims three or The Sims four? Do you build houses, or do you like to tell stories? Tell us in the comments, because we love reading your family stories. If you enjoyed this video, please subscribe and turn on notifications, because we have many more franchise histories coming. Thanks for watching, and we will see you in the next one.
